question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4
solution:
The correct answer is '**No**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage talks about the influence of public opinion on governments in a democracy.
 
• The chosen term should fit the logical flow of the sentence, highlighting that no government can resist strong public opinion for long.
 
• "**No**" is appropriate as it emphasizes the idea that not a single government can withstand the pressure of public opinion, aligning with the passage context.
 
• Other options ("**All**", "**Both**", "**Some**") do not convey the same meaning and do not fit the logical flow of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The newspaper is one of the significant signs of modern civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the present times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us both entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. No government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled together.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• All (सभी): "All" refers to every one without exception, which does not fit the context of emphasizing the inability of any single government to withstand public opinion.
 
• Both (दोनों): "Both" refers to two items, which does not fit the context of the sentence referring to a broader range.
 
• Some (कुछ): "Some" refers to a part of a larger group, which does not align with the sentence stressing the universal influence of public opinion on governments.
